description: Per-capita yearly means by country (carbon kg CO2e incl. land use, water withdrawals L, agricultural land m²·yr (world average, since territorial land misattributes food exporters), electricity demand kWh). The cohort model converts means to lognormal medians with median = mean·exp(−σ²/2). US states scale the US carbon mean by their production-based EIA ratio, clamped to [stateRatioMin, stateRatioMax].

usStates.note: EIA figures are production-based (power plants, refineries and industry that serve other states), so they spread far wider (MA 0.57×, WY 6.5× the US) than what residents consume; the ratio is clamped to 0.8–1.25× so a state baseline stays a plausible personal footprint.

citation.title: US EIA, Energy-related CO2 emissions by state, Table 4: per capita (2022)

sigmas.note: Carbon σ is narrower than WIR's ownership-based inequality (which attributes investment emissions to owners): a personal consumption footprint at σ 0.45 has its 10th–90th percentiles at 0.56×–1.78× the median (US ≈ 9–28 t).

citation.title: Chancel, Piketty et al., World Inequality Report 2022 (carbon inequality within countries); lognormal σ derived

Ivanova et al. (2016), Environmental Impact Assessment of Household Consumption, J. Ind. Ecol. 20:526
Underwood & Zahran (2015), The carbon implications of declining household scale, Ecological Economics 116:182

homeTypeModifiers.note: Household electricity use by housing type relative to the U.S. household average; dorms are taken as below apartments (shared, small, no major appliances).

citation.title: U.S. EIA, Residential Energy Consumption Survey (RECS) 2020: household electricity consumption by housing type

heatingModifiers.note: Household electricity use by main space-heating fuel relative to the U.S. household average: electrically heated homes draw more, fuel-heated homes less.

citation.title: U.S. EIA, Residential Energy Consumption Survey (RECS) 2020: household electricity consumption by main space-heating fuel
Ivanova et al. (2016), Environmental Impact Assessment of Household Consumption, J. Ind. Ecol. 20:526
